result.title: Learning When to Trust Medical Knowledge: Regression-Safe Routing for Clinical Reasoning
result.summary: Clinical reasoning LLMs need external medical knowledge, but retrieved evidence and reasoning chains can be outdated, poisoned, or hallucinated. Harmful knowledge can cause regression: changing a correct answer into an incorrect one. We construct a medical knowledge-poisoning benchmark covering retrieved evidence and reasoning chains, with seven attack families filtered by a three-judge "subtle-but-wrong" vote and paired clean exams that separate poisoning effects from question difficulty. No fixed knowledge-use strategy is robust across these settings: strong RAG methods trade robustness to poisoned evidence against accuracy when evidence is useful. We formulate knowledge use as per-instance routing and introduce Med-TrustRouter, a lightweight controller that keeps the solver frozen. From leakage-free runtime signals, it estimates each action's expected correctness gain and uncertainty, preserving the base answer unless another action is confidently better. Across seven medical reasoning settings, Med-TrustRouter achieves 78.9 macro and 69.2 worst-case accuracy, matching the strongest competitor on macro accuracy while substantially improving the worst-case floor. Its gains transfer across solvers and evidence judges, unlike a hand-coded router using the same signals. Similar performance across linear, tree, and neural action-value heads suggests that the benefit comes from routing rather than estimator complexity. These results support learning when to trust external knowledge for robust clinical reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建覆盖检索证据与推理链的医学知识投毒基准，并把「是否使用外部知识」形式化为逐实例路由；提出冻结求解器的轻量控制器 Med-TrustRouter，依据无泄漏运行时信号估计各动作的期望正确性增益与不确定性，仅在其他动作更有把握时改变答案，从而提升最差情形准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽为纯文本临床推理，其「采纳外部证据 vs 保留基线答案」的置信路由、期望增益与不确定性估计，可能为 LVR 的 LOOK/STOP 决策和视觉证据筛选提供借鉴；该机制能否迁移到多模态运行时信号尚待核查。
